## Part 1: Diabetes SQL practice
## Find the diabetes condition codes

## Finding conditions like diabetes. Notice the Quarto / R structure.
## Each chunk starts with ```{r} if you are writing in R, and includes a label
## and connection. We are saving SQL query results to R data frames by wrapping
## the query in df <- dbGetQuery(con, "QUERY")
## Close each chunk with ```.
```{r}
#| label: diabetes-codes
#| connection: con

diabetes_codes <- dbGetQuery(con, "select distinct
    DESCRIPTION
    , CODE
from
    conditions
where
    lower(DESCRIPTION) LIKE '%diab%'
order by
    DESCRIPTION
    ")
```

## Part 2: Preparing data for three charts
### Build `monthly_glucose_control`
### Build `glucose_by_insulin`


### Run chart (provided — do not edit)

```{r}
#| label: run-chart
#| connection: con

qic(
  x = month, y = numerator, n = denominator,
  data = monthly_glucose_control,
  chart = "run",
  title = "Glucose In Range \u2014 Run Chart"
)
```

### Control chart (provided — do not edit)

```{r}
#| label: control-chart
#| connection: con

qic(
  x = month, y = numerator, n = denominator,
  data = monthly_glucose_control,
  chart = "p",
  title = "Glucose In Range \u2014 Control Chart"
)
```

### ggplot (provided — do not edit)

```{r}
#| label: glucose-ggplot

ggplot(glucose_by_insulin, aes(x = glucose_date, y = glucose_value, color = insulin_status)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(75, 150), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  labs(
    title = "Glucose Readings by Insulin Status",
    x = "Date", y = "Glucose (mg/dL)", color = "Insulin status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
